title: Agreement Is Not Alignment: Divergent Moral Grounds in Human and LLM Ethical Judgments
abstract: arXiv:2608.12368v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agreement with human judgments is a common proxy for evaluating the alignment of large language models (LLMs). Yet agreement in final labels does not show that human annotators and models rely on the same moral grounds. Two agents may reach the same judgment while appealing to different principles, contextual assumptions, or interpretations of the situation.   We test this distinction using a curated 500-item ETHICS-derived benchmark spanning five domains of moral judgment, with new human annotator and LLM annotations of both final labels and supporting rationales. Across frontier and open model families, agreement with human annotator majority labels is often high. However, rationale-level analysis reveals systematic divergence in the moral grounds expressed by human annotators and models. translated_title: 一致并非对齐：人类与LLM道德判断中的分歧道德基础
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.12368v1 公告类型：新 摘要：与人类判断的一致性是评估大型语言模型（LLMs）对齐程度的一种常见代理指标。然而，最终标签上的一致并不能表明人类标注者和模型依赖相同的道德基础。两个智能体可能得出相同的判断，但依据的原则、情境假设或对情况的理解却不同。我们使用一个精选的、包含500个项目的ETHICS衍生基准来测试这一区别，该基准涵盖五个道德判断领域，并包含新的人类标注者和LLM对最终标签及支持理由的注释。在前沿和开放模型家族中，与人类标注者多数标签的一致性通常很高。然而，理由层面的分析揭示了人类标注者和模型所表达道德基础的系统性分歧。特别是，模型在伤害、尊重、守诺、正义、应得和借口相关性等类别上重新分配了关注度，即使在标签一致的情况下也是如此。
tldr: 这项研究通过对比人类和LLM在道德判断中的最终标签与支持理由，揭示了高一致性可能掩盖道德基础的系统性分歧，表明“一致”并不等于真正的“对齐”。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that high agreement between human and LLM ethical judgments can mask systematic divergence in underlying moral grounds, showing that agreement does not equate to true alignment.
